questions.q: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The Survey showed that across most tasks
basic numeracy and reading skills
questions.s:
Solution:

  • Explanation:

  • The word "best" is the superlative form of "good" and is used when comparing more than two.

  • "The Survey showed that across most tasks" – correctly structured.

"The Survey showed that across most tasks that test the ability to apply basic numeracy and reading skills, Primary school boys did better than girls."

questions.q:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

The childrens' toys were scattered all over the floor, making the entire room look very untidy.
questions.s:
The error is in the formation of the possessive noun "childrens'". The noun 'child' is an irregular noun; its plural form is 'children', not 'childs' or 'childrens'. To make a plural noun that does not end in '-s' possessive, we add an apostrophe and an 's' ('s). Therefore, the correct possessive form is "children's". "Childrens'" is incorrect as it implies the plural is 'childrens', which is wrong.

The correct sentence is: The children's toys were scattered all over the floor, making the entire room look very untidy.

Hence, option (c) is the correct answer.

Note:

Possessive nouns: are types of nouns that show ownership or connection. All nouns become possessive nouns with the addition of an apostrophe and a suffix - the letter "s" - at the end of the word. However, when a plural noun ends in the letter "s," the possessive form of the word only requires the use of an apostrophe at the end. Possessive nouns can be tricky because they function like adjectives by modifying another noun or pronoun in the sentence. E.g., "Timmy's dog is cute."

questions.q: Select the grammatically correct sentence.
o: Rajat have been working on this project for two weeks.
Rajat has been working on this project for two weeks.
Rajat has been working on this project since two weeks.
Rajat have been working on this project since two weeks.
questions.s:
The sentence given in option (b) is grammatically correct.

Options (a) and (d) are incorrect because of the subject-verb agreement issue. The subject "Rajat" is singular, so the correct verb form should be the singular "has" instead of plural "have".

Option (c) is also incorrect. The phrase "since two weeks" is incorrect. The word "since" is used to refer to a specific point in time when an action started. It is typically followed by a specific point in time (e.g., since Monday, since June). It is not used to indicate a duration of time like "two weeks". The correct preposition to use here is "for". "For" is used to indicate the duration of time something has been happening. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

The correct sentence is: Rajat has been working on this project for two weeks.

NOTE:

A Preposition is a word placed before a noun or a pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition) and shows a relationship in space or time or a logical relationship between two or more people, places, or things in a sentence.

Examples

I. The teacher scolded the child for being late.

II. We're going to a party.

· The words in bold are called prepositions because they normally take position before (pre) a noun/pronoun or a noun equivalent (pronoun, adverb, gerund, infinitive, adverbial clause, or any clause that can be used as the object of the preposition.

· The noun/pronoun which is used with a preposition is called its Object.

Subject-verb agreement means that a subject and its verb must be both singular or both plural:

A singular subject takes a singular verb.

A plural subject takes a plural verb.

For example, in the sentence 'John lives in France', the subject John (singular 'he') 'agrees with' the third person singular form of the verb to live - lives.
